claims.claim: the Atacama's core averages under 1 millimetre of rain per year, and some weather stations have never recorded meaningful rainfall
claims.definition: the hyperarid core of the Atacama Desert in northern Chile: rain gauges at stations such as Calama and parts of Antofagasta province stay at or near zero year after year

nuance.note: the desert's margins do receive occasional rain; the under-1-mm figure applies to the hyperarid core, not the whole region

sources: multiple station records compiled in Atacama hyperaridity literature

claims.claim: the Andes block Amazon moisture from the east while the cold Humboldt Current and a persistent Pacific anticyclone suppress rain from the west
claims.definition: a double rain shadow: mountain barrier to one side, cold-ocean stabilization plus high-pressure subsidence to the other

nuance.note: the anticyclone's subsidence warms and dries descending air; the cold current chills marine air so it resists convective rain

claims.claim: fog oases called lomas form green ribbons on coastal ridgelines between roughly 300 and 1,000 metres elevation
claims.definition: lomas vegetacionales: vegetation patches inside the coastal fog band, found from Peru to northern Chile; individual lomas host dozens to over a hundred plant species

nuance.note: the exact band shifts with latitude and season; species counts vary strongly between individual lomas sites

sources: lomas ecosystem literature (e.g. Lomas Paposo, Pan de Azúcar surveys)

claims.claim: the camanchaca is a coastal fog deck that forms where air crosses the cold Humboldt Current and is capped by a warm-air inversion, typically below about 1,000 metres
claims.definition: warm, dry air over cold upwelled water produces low marine stratocumulus fog; the inversion lid keeps it from growing into rain clouds, so it moves inland as fog instead

nuance.note: the deck's height varies seasonally; rain still occurs rarely at the desert margins

claims.claim: standard fog collectors in prime Atacama fog zones harvest roughly 2 to 5 litres of water per square metre of mesh per day
claims.definition: flat mesh fog collectors (atrapanieblas) intercept fog droplets that coalesce, run down, and drain to storage; yields swing with fog frequency and wind
claims.measured_value: 2–5 L/m²/day typical; arrays of ~100 m² can reach hundreds of litres per day

nuance.note: yields drop toward zero in fog-free stretches; published figures span wide ranges by site and season

sources: published fog-harvesting studies in Chañaral and Peña Blanca, Chile

claims.claim: NASA and astrobiologists use the Atacama's Yungay core as a Mars analog because its soils are among the driest on Earth
claims.definition: in the Yungay region, soil moisture and organic content fall so low that instrument teams test life-detection hardware there before sending it to Mars
claims.measured_value: decades of instrument testing in Yungay

nuance.note: even Yungay is not perfectly sterile; it approximates, not replicates, Martian surface conditions

sources: NASA ASTEP / Mars-analog field campaigns in the Atacama
